Glowing clouds, strangely coloured lightning and weather that shifts every half hour or so while the sky changes colour. Carried radios crackle with noise. Any time of year.

The whole sky turns deep red, everything takes on an eerie red tint and a powerful windstorm blows in. The dead grow restless: zombies for a long way around are drawn towards the living and come straight for you. Any time of year.

Strange electrical disturbances: carried radios cut out in bursts of static, flashlights die, car engines stall and headlights go out, and car and building alarms go off on their own. Pale flashes light the sky. Any time of year.

A massive wildfire with its own weather: a black and orange sky, flaming debris falling, winds that spread embers far ahead into buildings and whole neighbourhoods, and smoke that kills without a mask or respirator. Part way through a fire cloud forms: lightning and sudden wind shifts swing the front around. June to October.

Torrential rain, then rising water. After up to an hour of rain the flood rises over up to two hours, floods streets and houses up to the depth set below, then drains away when the storm ends. Deep water exhausts and can drown you.

A towering wall of dust races across the map towards you. The sky browns as it nears; once it hits, it is dark as night and you can barely see. Outdoor generators clog and car engines choke on the dust. May to September.
Freezing rain coats everything in ice: branches snap and fall, trees come down, the power lines fail part way through, cars skid and walking (worse, running) outside means falling. November to March.

A sudden blast of descending air slams into a small area with almost no warning: trees and fences come down, cars are shoved sideways, weak roofs are damaged and anyone caught in it is knocked flat. Short (20-40 minutes) unless given its own length below. May to September.

An enormous outbreak spawns several tornadoes (number below) one after another over several hours, every strength from thin EF1 ropes to giant EF5 wedges. The siren sounds before each touchdown. Lasts as long as its tornadoes need unless given its own length. March to June.

A rotating monster storm under a greenish sky and a low wall cloud: enormous hail (umbrellas don't help), damaging winds, lightning, and sometimes it drops one of the mod's tornadoes (chance below). March to August.

A rare 7-day superstorm over the whole map. Day 1 violent thunderstorms and power failure, day 2 floods, day 3 straight-line winds, day 4 tornadoes, day 5 bitter cold, day 6 extreme wind and flooding, day 7 it weakens. Length 7 game days unless given its own length (split into seven 'days'). Very rare, any time of year.

Hot, dry, windy days when a fire front sweeps in from the countryside, burning grass and trees and anything in its way, buildings included. Needs the vanilla fire spread option on to spread beyond the front. June to October.
Longest a firestorm lasts, in game hours (168 = 7 days). 0 = its usual length.
Shortest a firestorm lasts, in game hours. 0 = its usual length.
No extreme weather before this many days have passed.
Cars standing in floodwater about half a metre deep or more slowly lose engine condition, parked or driven.

How high the water rises at the height of a flash flood, in centimetres (steps of 25). 50 = knee deep, 100 = waist deep, 150 = chest deep, 200 = over your head, 290 = ground floors fill and water runs over single-storey roofs.
Floodwater drains your body heat - the deeper you stand, the faster. Stay in it long enough and you get hypothermia. Get out, get dry and warm up.
Longest a flash flood lasts, in game hours (72 = 3 days). 0 = use the general maximum storm length.
Shortest a flash flood lasts, in game hours. 0 = use the general minimum storm length.
Clothes under the waterline get soaked through, muddy and slowly worn down while you wade.
Flash flood: water drawn around you (tiles)
How far from each player the floodwater is drawn. Higher hides the edge of the water at wider zoom levels but costs more performance (and network traffic on a server).

The server lays the standing water of a flash flood around every player and sends it to everyone, so all players see the same flood. Off: players still get the puddles, rain, wading, deep water and a murky screen tint. Floating debris is single-player only. Single-player always shows the water.
Haboob: dust clogs generators and engines

How much lightning an electrical storm throws down around each player. 1 = about one and a half strikes per game minute at full strength, 0.5 = half that, 0 = none.
Electrical storm: chance to be struck (percent per hour)

Chance per game hour, at full storm strength, that lightning hits a player standing outside. A hit knocks you down and burns you. Indoors and in vehicles you are safe. 0 = lightning never hits players.
Microburst: knocks down fences and damages roofs
Off: trees still fall and cars are still shoved.

Adds an 'Extreme Weather' entry to the right-click menu to start or stop storms. Always shown to admins and in single-player debug mode. In multiplayer only admins (and the co-op host) see it.
Chance per in-game day that an extreme weather event begins (rolled hourly).
Ice storms and the global superstorm bring the power grid down while they last (only while the grid is still on). It comes back when the storm ends.

Shortest a supercell thunderstorm lasts, in game hours. 0 = its usual length.
Chance that a supercell drops a tornado part way through.

Shortest a global superstorm lasts, in game hours. 0 = its usual length.

Tornadoes tear apart what they pass over, scaled by strength: EF1 knocks down fences, EF2 starts on roofs and loose objects, EF3 rips off roofs and upper floors, EF4 brings down many walls, EF5 levels buildings to the foundations. Includes player-built bases. The damage is permanent.
Tornadoes roll EF1 35 percent, EF2 28, EF3 20, EF4 12, EF5 5 within this range. EF3+ rip off doors and wreck cars, EF4+ uproot trees, EF5 flattens player-built walls and fences.
Longest a tornado lasts, in game hours (72 = 3 days). 0 = use the general maximum storm length. With both left at 0 a tornado never lasts more than 3 hours.
Shortest a tornado lasts, in game hours. 0 = use the general minimum storm length.
EF2+ tornadoes can lift players on foot who get into the funnel, spin them around and throw them clear. Landing damage and fracture chance scale with the EF rating.
A player thrown by a tornado can die on landing: EF3 10 percent, EF4 40 percent, EF5 85 percent. Off = landings only injure.
Tornadoes destroy everything in their path

On: every tornado, EF1 to EF5, flattens everything its funnel passes over - walls, roofs, every upper floor, fences, furniture, doors and trees - and wrecks the vehicles in it. The wider the funnel, the wider the path. Crops are spared. Off: the damage depends on the EF rating (see the option above). Buildings also need Tornadoes destroy buildings on.

Vehicles in the funnel get picked up and thrown by its winds, trucks and cars with people driving or sitting in them included, more the bigger the tornado: EF1 hops them off the ground, EF2 lifts and spins them, EF3 rolls them, EF4 throws them and EF5 throws them high. Heavier vehicles move less.
EF2+ tornadoes sweep up zombies outdoors in the funnel, spin them around and throw them out. Stronger tornadoes kill more of them on landing; survivors may be left crawling.
In-game minutes between the emergency broadcast and the storm hitting.
Longest a wildfire lasts, in game hours (72 = 3 days). 0 = use the general maximum storm length.
Shortest a wildfire lasts, in game hours. 0 = use the general minimum storm length.
Your radio crackles with strange noise...
The engine and lights cut out!
The car is under water - get out and swim for higher ground!
Floodwater is pouring into the car!
The floodwater is freezing - get out and get dry!
The water is up to your chest!
You're out of your depth - get upstairs or to higher ground!
A fire cloud has formed - lightning and sudden wind shifts!
Extreme Weather menu is admin-only in multiplayer
Run storm self-test (about 7 min, stand outside)
The car skids on the ice!
The smoke is suffocating you - get a mask!
EMERGENCY BROADCAST: %1 WARNING - arrives in %2 min
The wind nearly knocks you over!
Corrosive rain. Wear a poncho or carry an umbrella.
Unexplained atmospheric activity. Radio interference expected. Stay calm and stay indoors.
Lethal cold. Wrap up warm and find shelter and heat.
The sky has turned red and the dead are restless. Barricade, stay quiet and do not go out alone.
Flash flooding. Stay dry, stay warm, stay inside.
Near-zero visibility. Cover your mouth and stay hydrated.
Lightning strikes imminent. Do not stay in the open.
Electronics failing. Expect radios, flashlights and vehicles to cut out and alarms to sound.
Firestorm. Smoke is lethal: wear a mask or respirator. Evacuate away from the fire and the wind.
Rising water. Water may reach rooftops. Move upstairs or to higher ground and stay out of the current.
A wall of dust is approaching. Get indoors, cover your mouth, shelter your equipment.
Stay indoors. A helmet or umbrella will protect you outside.
Extreme heat. Drink water and stay out of the sun.
Freezing rain. Roads and paths are glass. Do not run, do not drive, expect power cuts.
Sudden violent downdraft. Get indoors immediately and away from trees.
Multiple tornadoes expected over several hours. Shelter and stay sheltered until the all-clear.
Fallout! Shelter indoors. Gas mask, NBC mask or hazmat suit required outside.
Rotating thunderstorm with giant hail and possible tornadoes. Shelter in a sturdy building now.
A superstorm will cover the whole region for a week. Stock up, shelter, and do not travel.
Take shelter in a sturdy building away from windows. Do not outrun it on foot in the open.
A wildfire is spreading through the area with the wind. Get clear of trees and grass, cover your mouth and do not get caught downwind.
